sum: A week's loop from Syabrubesi through the Tamang villages of Gatlang, Tatopani, Thuman and Briddim, with homestay nights and a 3,165 m viewpoint at Nagthali.

guide.note: Thuman and Timure are on the Department of Immigration's restricted-area list, so this loop is treated here as a restricted-area trek: the permit is issued only through a registered trekking agency and you must walk with a licensed guide. Since 22 March 2026 the permit can be issued to a single trekker. Checks on the ground have been rare and some agencies run the loop on the park permit and TIMS alone, so ask yours what it arranges. After the 2026 flood a guide in touch with the villages is also the only reliable source on which bridges and homestays are open.

access: By road to Syabrubesi, the same seven to nine hour journey from Machhapokhari in Kathmandu as for the Langtang valley. The Bhote Koshi flood of 26 August 2026 cut the road short of the town and took out the bridges over the river. The loop was reported open again later that autumn, once a temporary footbridge had been built at Syabrubesi, but the road was still reported closed in mid-November 2026. Ask your agency how groups are reaching the start.

photo.a: The closely packed stone houses of Gatlang sit among terraced fields on a hillside, with a track winding up to the village below a steep forested slope.

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Langtang National Park permit and TIMS card
homestay or lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or jeep from Kathmandu and back

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

permits.name: Rasuwa (Thuman and Timure) restricted area permit
permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.

transportText: Bus or a jeep seat between Kathmandu and the Langtang roadhead, each way
tips: In a homestay you eat what the family cooks, at the family's hours. Agree the price for bed and meals when you arrive.
Carry all the cash you need, in small notes. There is no ATM on the loop and nobody can change large bills.
Ask in Gatlang whether the Tatopani pools have water before you count on a soak.
Dress modestly in the villages, and ask before photographing people, houses or the inside of a monastery.
Bring a light sleeping bag or liner. Homestay bedding is clean but thin, and nights at Tatopani and Nagthali are cold.

days.note: A long road day through Trishuli Bazaar and Dhunche, where park permits are checked. Since the August 2026 flood the road has been cut short of Syabrubesi, so the last stretch may be on foot; settle the plan with your agency before you leave Kathmandu.

Climb steeply west out of the valley for two hours to the Rongga Bhanjyang saddle and its view of Ganesh Himal, then contour through Goljung to Gatlang. Much of the old trail now shares a dirt road; a guide knows the footpath shortcuts. If you arrive early, walk up to Parvati Kunda above the village.

Descend through terraced fields to Thambuchet and Chilime on the Chilime Khola, cross the suspension bridge, and climb about 850 m through Gonggang to Tatopani. The climb is on an open, south-facing slope, so carry more water than you think you need. Ask on arrival whether the hot-spring pools have water.

Up through forest to the hamlet of Brimdang and on to the meadows of Nagthali for the widest view of the trek, then a steep 800 m descent through rhododendron forest to Thuman. Some groups sleep at Nagthali for the sunrise instead.

Classically a 600 m descent to the Bhote Koshi, a crossing to the valley road near Lingling and a hot 500 m climb to Briddim. The August 2026 flood ran straight through this section and took bridges and road with it; which line you walk depends on what has been rebuilt, so settle it with your guide in Thuman.

A short morning downhill through terraces and forest to the valley floor and the river crossing into Syabrubesi. If you are going on into the Langtang valley, take the high trail from Briddim through Khangjim and Sherpagaon to Rimche instead.
Back up to the highway and down through Dhunche and Trishuli Bazaar. Timings on this road are unpredictable, so keep the evening and the following morning clear of fixed commitments.
